drivers: Recovery balance is negative (implied by high Z4% this month and low Z1% vs last month — 26% vs 43%), ACWR likely elevated (Z4 jumped from 8% to 31% while Z1 collapsed), aerobic TE increased from 2.6 to 3.0 indicating reduced fatigue resistance, resting HR trend not provided but avg HR rose from 134 to 139 bpm across months suggesting autonomic stress, sleep and HRV data absent but recovery balance and load distribution strongly suggest under-recovery
readiness.guidance: This week must prioritise nervous system restoration — no intensity, minimal volume, and emphasis on parasympathetic activation.

monthly_review.summary: Running volume dropped sharply (29.5 km vs 51.3 km), pace improved slightly but at the cost of higher HR and aerobic decoupling, and zone distribution shifted dramatically toward high-intensity work with a collapse in easy-zone running.
monthly_review.highlight: The 31% of time spent in Zone 4 this month — up from just 8% last month and 18% in July — is not part of a progressive build but an acute, unbalanced shift that coincides with rising aerobic decoupling and falling efficiency.

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s 51.3 km would require ~21.8 km across 4 remaining sessions — averaging over 5.4 km/session — but given compromised readiness, chasing this volume risks injury or stagnation; recovery, not mileage, is the priority for the next 18 days.

insights.title: Zone 4 dominance without supporting base
insights.body: Z4 now accounts for 31% of all run time — triple last month’s 8% and higher than July’s 18% — yet Z1 dropped to 26% (vs 43% in August), indicating a collapse in true recovery running and likely insufficient stimulus for mitochondrial biogenesis.

insights.title: Worsening running economy tracks with cadence drop and HR rise
insights.body: Avg efficiency worsened to 14.56 ml/kg/km (from 14.12) while avg cadence fell 13 spm (149 → 136) and avg HR rose 5 bpm — suggesting compensatory recruitment of less efficient motor units due to fatigue or poor neuromuscular recovery.

insights.title: Aerobic decoupling increased despite slower average pace
insights.body: Avg aerobic TE rose to 3.0% (from 2.6% in August) even though average pace slowed (524 → 534 sec/km last month), meaning cardiovascular drift occurred earlier and more severely — a classic sign of accumulated fatigue, not fitness gain.

insights.title: Ground contact time divergence signals fatigue asymmetry
insights.body: Recent runs show wide GC variability: 282 ms (Sep 3) vs 389 ms (Sep 1) vs 327 ms (Sep 6) — a 107 ms swing — while vertical oscill rose to 9.2% (Sep 3), suggesting neuromuscular instability and reduced elastic recoil, likely tied to insufficient recovery between hard efforts.

recommendations.action: Zone 1 only: 4.0 km, HR ≤ 120 bpm, on Tuesday — walk breaks permitted if HR exceeds threshold
recommendations.reason: Restores autonomic balance, rebuilds Z1 tolerance, and counters recent Z4 overload without adding strain

recommendations.action: Complete 20 min supine diaphragmatic breathing + 10 min foam rolling quads/IT band, both evenings Wednesday and Friday
recommendations.reason: Directly targets elevated sympathetic tone (evident in HR creep and aerobic TE) and supports tissue recovery in absence of HRV/sleep metrics

recommendations.action: Zero running Thursday, Saturday, Sunday — replace with 30-min brisk walk (HR 110–125 bpm) on Sunday only
recommendations.reason: Forces systemic recovery days while maintaining light circulatory stimulus; avoids compounding fatigue from recent high-Z4 density

risk_flags.evidence: Z4% spiked to 31% (vs 8% last month), aerobic TE increased to 3.0%, efficiency declined to 14.56, and cadence dropped 13 spm — all converging signs of maladaptation rather than adaptation
risk_flags.action: Remove all Z3+ efforts for minimum 10 days; reassess after two full Z1 weeks

risk_flags.evidence: Ground contact time range of 282–389 ms across last 5 runs and vertical oscill spiking to 9.2% (Sep 3) indicate deteriorating movement economy and potential compensation patterns
risk_flags.action: Pause all speedwork and hill efforts until GC stabilises within 25 ms range for 3 consecutive runs

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish autonomic control, restore stride consistency, and rebuild tolerance for low-intensity effort — not to 'do less', but to retrain the body’s response to load.
